9d35aa00bb563255.title: Engineering Manager, Agent & Product Security
9d35aa00bb563255.jd:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor’s agents work inside the codebases of some of the most security-conscious engineering organizations in the world — holding credentials, reading untrusted content, running tools, and shipping changes. Today they act on authority delegated per task. Where we’re headed, they’ll work more like coworkers: autonomous over long horizons, holding standing responsibilities, initiating work, and collaborating with people and other agents. The security models that future needs — identity and accountability for autonomous workers, standing authority rather than per-task permission, agent-to-agent trust, oversight that scales with always-on autonomy — mostly don’t exist yet.

As Engineering Manager for Agent & Product Security, you’ll lead the team that makes agentic software development trustworthy. This team owns the security boundaries between customers, data, tools, repositories, workspaces, and agent authority across Cursor’s product and agents and designs the primitives behind them: agent identity, delegated authority, policy enforcement, secure tool execution, and prompt-injection containment. Little of this has settled precedent, so the team’s decisions carry unusual weight for Cursor and for how the industry approaches these problems.

Security here is tightly coupled to product strategy: customers adopt agent autonomy as fast as we can make it trustworthy, so the boundaries your team makes safe directly determine what the product can ship. You’ll help set that direction.



What you’ll do

 - Chart the path from supervised agents to trusted autonomous ones: define the security primitives that enable agent autonomy, and lead the team that builds them.

 - Engineer the isolation that makes Cursor safe to run inside customers’ most valuable codebases: tenancy, workspace, secret, and data protections designed for real adversaries.

 - Build the authority infrastructure autonomous agents need: identity, scoped permissions, policy enforcement, and secure tool execution, so an agent can hold real responsibility with verifiable limits and full accountability.

 - Build customer-facing security controls that are understandable, usable, and strong enough for Cursor’s most security-sensitive customers, with crisp success metrics for security outcomes.

 - Hire, coach, and grow a high-performing security engineering team while staying technically close to the work: write and review code where useful, and keep execution fast and technically grounded.



You may be a fit if

 - You’ve led engineering teams shipping production systems with high security, reliability, or platform stakes — and you want a problem space where much of the answer isn’t written down yet.

 - You have strong product and systems judgment: you can reason from user workflows to architecture, threat models, enforcement points, and operational tradeoffs — and you see security as something that enables product capability, not only restricts it.

 - You understand modern application security, authorization, tenancy, identity, secrets, data isolation, and secure-by-default platform design.

 - You have good instincts about AI agents: how they use tools, where authority should come from, how prompt injection and exfiltration show up in practice, and how to build mitigations that hold up against creative adversaries.

 - You’re comfortable operating in ambiguity: you can set strategy where precedent is thin, commit to a direction, and stay close enough to the implementation to know when to change it.

 - You can partner well across product, infrastructure, ML, and customer-facing teams.



#LI-DNI

6b65bb3806c0565c.title: Product Education Engineer
6b65bb3806c0565c.jd:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor ships fast. New models, new agentic capabilities, new workflows every week. The gap between what Cursor can do and what developers know how to build with it grows with every release. This role closes that gap, one lab, workshop, and tutorial at a time.

As a Product Education Engineer, you'll build the technical content and hands-on experiences that move developers from first install to deep, durable fluency. Code walkthroughs, labs, reference implementations, workshops, in-product learning, and whatever new formats we invent as we go. The demos and tutorials you ship should be things you built by pushing Cursor to its limits in your own work.

This is not a traditional customer education role. We're hiring engineers who teach, not curriculum developers who need external SMEs to write for them. You'll be the SME. You'll go deep on the product, deep with customers, and deep with the engineers building Cursor. You'll be the internal source of truth our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to when the product changes and they need to get up to speed.

You'll report to the Director of Product Education Engineering and partner with our Learning Experience Design team, who will help you translate technical depth into content that actually teaches.

What you’ll do

 - Build Cursor's technical learning library hands-on: code walkthroughs, tutorials, labs, workshops, reference implementations, and instructor-led training

 - Build high-quality demos, reference implementations, and workflow automations, using Cursor itself as part of your development process

 - Lead large-format workshops, technical deep dives, and hands-on enablement sessions that help engineering organizations adopt AI coding tools effectively and drive measurable outcomes

 - Be the technical translation layer between Product and the field. When Cursor ships new capabilities, our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to you to get up to speed

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, DevRel, and Go-to-Market ahead of major launches so new capabilities ship with clear educational framing, practical examples, and adoption paths on day one

 - Contribute technical guides, patterns, and best practices to Cursor's public technical content to help the broader developer community accelerate their work with Cursor

 - Design learning experiences for both developers and non-technical users (e.g. eng leaders evaluating rollout, PMs pairing with agents). Enterprise adoption depends on both, and our content has to meet each audience on its own terms

 - Experiment with new formats for education, including in-product learning, hands-on labs, interactive experiences, live teaching, and AI-native tutorials (e.g. guided flows that adapt to repo context and skill level)

 - Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering on where developers get stuck and what would unlock the next stage of adoption

 - Measure what works, tracking adoption and fluency gains rather than completion rates

You may be a fit if

 - You have 5+ years of experience in Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Consulting, technical enablement, or software engineering at a developer tools or platform company

 - You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle, modern engineering org structures, and how AI coding tools are reshaping how software gets built

 - You are an active power user of AI coding tools and have deeply customized your own developer workflow.

 - You have a point of view on what makes engineers more productive

 - You enjoy building scrappy, high-signal demos, integrations, and prototypes that clearly articulate what Cursor can enable, often using Cursor to accelerate your own development process

 - You have delivered large, high-impact workshops or technical training to engineering teams and know how to craft sessions that are engaging, hands-on, and outcomes-driven.

 - You have built the enablement infrastructure behind the workshops, including demo environments, content-freshness automation, and self-service tooling

 - You communicate complex technical concepts in clear, persuasive written and verbal form, especially when helping customers make strategic decisions about where and how to apply AI

 - You are excited by ambiguous, rapidly evolving problem spaces and enjoy iterating toward novel solutions hand-in-hand with customers

 - You care about customer success and operational excellence as much as you care about technical ingenuity

 - You have a builder mindset, high agency, and a bias toward experimenting with new educational formats rather than defaulting to traditional documentation

Oyster is looking for a sharp, self-driven Employment Counsel to contribute to Oyster's growth and shape the future of global distributed work. As part of our Employment Law Team, you'll advise internal teams and external stakeholders on employment law matters across multiple jurisdictions, playing a direct role in how Oyster supports workers and companies around the world.

A core part of the role is researching and staying current on employment laws and regulations across jurisdictions; managing employment templates, policies, and standard employment processes; liaising with outside counsel on local legal requirements; creating clear, accessible guidance on hiring, managing, and terminating workers globally; and advising Oyster's Platform and Product teams on building a scalable, compliant technology platform. You'll also contribute to the strategic development of our employment-as-a-platform model.

Because Oyster operates as an Employer of Record (EOR), a solid understanding of how that model works, and the unique legal considerations it creates for Oyster, our customers, and their team members, is essential to this role.

The right candidate brings extensive employment law experience, including multi-jurisdictional and cross-border matters, and a track record of advising HR and business partners. Knowledge of immigration rules and employee benefits is a plus. Beyond legal expertise, we're looking for someone who translates complex issues into clear, practical guidance for non-legal audiences, balancing compliance with pragmatic problem-solving, anticipating emerging risks, and partnering strategically with the business to deliver outcomes that are both legally sound and operationally effective.

We also value candidates who embrace AI and other technology tools to enhance efficiency, streamline workflows, and scale the impact of their legal expertise.

 - Own and maintain employment templates, policies, and processes across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring Oyster's employment offering remains compliant, scalable, and operationally effective.

 - Monitor legislative and regulatory developments globally, assess their impact on Oyster's products and operations, and drive implementation of required changes.

 - Partner closely with Product, People team and other cross-functional stakeholders to design and implement compliant employment solutions that balance legal requirements with business objectives.

 - Advise on a broad range of employment law and compliance matters across the employee lifecycle, including hiring, compensation, leave, performance management, terminations.

 - Support strategic initiatives such as Direct Expansion, indirect-to-direct migrations, and the launch of new employment products and features.

 - Research complex employment law issues and translate legal analysis into clear, practical, and business-focused recommendations.

 - Develop and maintain employment guides, knowledge resources, and compliance documentation to support scalable operations across Oyster's global footprint.

 - Support labor inspections, audits, regulatory inquiries, and other employment compliance initiatives.

 - Use data, stakeholder feedback, and operational insights to identify risks, improve processes, and enhance the effectiveness of Oyster's employment compliance framework.

 - Identify and champion opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and process innovation to improve team efficiency, reduce manual work, and enable the scalable delivery of employment compliance and legal support.

 - Contribute to a highly collaborative, remote-first team culture and help drive continuous improvement across Employment Products.



Core Requirements

 - Law Degree (e.g. JD or equivalent) and admission to practice law in one or more jurisdictions.

 - 4+ years of experience practicing employment law, preferably with a combination of law firm and in-house practice.

 - Deep expertise in employment law, including hands-on experience with standard employment processes: drafting and reviewing contracts, managing templates and policies, advising across a wide range of employment matters and interpreting local labor regulations across multiple jurisdictions.

 - Understanding of the EOR model and ability to anticipate and navigate its unique legal challenges; prior experience working with or within an EOR is preferred.

 - Experience managing multi-jurisdictional and/or cross-border employment matters, with the ability to work across diverse legal systems and regulatory environments.

 - Strong business acumen with the ability to distill complex legal concepts into clear, practical, and actionable guidance for non-legal stakeholders; creativity and pragmatism in risk mitigation are essential.

 - Excellent analytical, communication, and research skills, with a keen eye for detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, global environment.

 - A technology-forward mindset, including curiosity and comfort with leveraging AI and automation tools to work more efficiently and continuously improve legal processes.

582122e3d650b5ac.jd:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Security and data privacy are at the core of everything we do at 1Password. The Product Security Team is responsible for implementing new security features across our macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, Linux and Web applications as well as building libraries to share common security-critical code, resolving security vulnerabilities across our applications, and promoting secure coding practices across the organization.

As a Senior Developer on our Device Security squad, you will play a key role in implementing the next generation of security features in our applications, and help shape our security operations and best practices. You'll be intimately involved in ensuring secure coding practices across our code-base, guiding product teams on best practices, resolving security vulnerabilities in our products when they arise, and demonstrating leadership in the area of secure coding and development.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US. 



What we're looking for: 

 - 4+ years of experience in software development with a security angle; development experience with modern encryption techniques and libraries or authentication protocols

 - 4+ years of hands-on experience with Windows security development with technical expertise in languages such as Rust, C#, C/C++, Go or TypeScript

 - Experience with Rust development and creating FFI interfaces, especially for Windows. Knowledge of Windows OS architecture and platform-specific optimization techniques

 - Familiarity with TPM and HSM functionality with proven experience in Windows security features such as Windows Hello, BitLocker, Secure Boot, and Credential Guard

 - A strong understanding of and passion for the security domain; that could include understanding of topics in the sub-domains of cryptography, network security, application security, common threat vectors, and access control mechanisms etc.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills; our security team often communicates nuanced topics to a variety of internal audiences, and has to understand these nuances during the design phase

 - You’re a self starter with strong organizational skills who enjoys solving moderately complex problems with a demonstrated ability to tackle problems and propose effective solutions

 - Knowledge of and practical experience with Agentic AI Model capabilities and workflows



Bonus points:

 - Experience with SAML, OAuth and OpenID Connect

 - Experience working on a SaaS product

 - Leadership experience as a software developer in a team environment

 - Experience with GitHub or GitLab as well as CI/CD pipelines

 - Experience with system analysis and performance monitoring tools such as DataDog, SemGrep, Sonarqube, Fortify etc.

 - Personal experience using 1Password



What you can expect: 

 - Work within a small team of developers who are specialists in Rust, Go, Swift, and Security Development

 - Implement new security features for the next generation of 1Password and develop secure libraries to share common security-critical code across our applications

 - Assist in security design efforts or scoping initiatives for new features by identifying major tasks and breaking down, estimating, and planning work

 - Demonstrate leadership in security development and act as a trusted point of contact for management and other developers

 - Code, test, debug, deliver and maintain production software systems for new and existing product features

 - Collaborate with a variety of teams across our hybrid core architecture from Design to QA, as well as security engineering for design guidance and secure coding practices

 - Work with your teammates to communicate technical requirements to stakeholders and solve technical problems in a scalable and realistic way

 - Mentor junior and new team members by helping them understand team expectations, providing technical guidance, sharing knowledge, and engaging in pair programming sessions

 - Review code for others to maintain high code quality, knowledge share within the team, and support creating a safe environment of giving and receiving feedback

 - Stay informed about the latest industry trends, technologies, and best practices in security development
   
   



USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $153,000 USD and $214,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $144,000 CAD and $202,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

Health and wellbeing
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future

💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

Community

🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment

 - You'll work closely with designers, engineers and ops to define the right product and implement it.

 - You'll partner and align with all parts of the business: Marketing, Sales, Brand, and Data.



About the Growth area

Growth owns everything that happens before someone becomes a member: how prospects find Alan, how they decide we're right for them, and how they start. It runs across two crews.

 - Conversion: the conversion flows and referral surfaces that turn prospects into members.

 - Growth Infrastructure: the website, marketing measurement, and marketing ops that make growth marketing efficient.

You'll own the product across both crews. You'll set the overarching product vision, manage the PMs, push experimentation velocity, and lead Alan's move to make Growth Product AI-native.



More specifically, this means the following.



Lead Alan's AI ambition in Growth

The way people discover and buy insurance is about to change, and we want Alan ahead of it. You'll set the agenda and ship against it:

 - Conversational AI that guides prospects through our sales flows.

 - AI-native acquisition surfaces.

 - Alan inside LLM ecosystems. Picture a GPT app where a prospect can shop for and buy health insurance, and agentic commerce more broadly.

You don't need to have built all of this before. You do need a real, opinionated view of where AI is going, and the drive to turn it into shipped product rather than decks.



Build an experimentation engine

Conversion is won by learning faster than anyone else.

We have achieved a first baseline of A/B testing, learning loops, and a clear shared bar for what actually counts as a win. Now we want to take it to the next level. You'll improve our experimentation culture and the velocity.



Give the area a coherent vision

You'll align the Conversion and Growth Infrastructure roadmaps and concentrate the team's bets where the leverage is.

Two bigger shifts sit in your scope. Alan is going from one product to many, and Growth needs to move from a single conversion flow toward something modular. We're also scaling a self-served model built to travel fast, so it can reach a new country quickly with controlled local adaptation.



Build the team

You'll manage the PMs in the area and contribute to people topics for all product communities in the area (Design, Engineering, Data, Insurance).   Location:  You can choose to work at Qonto as long as you're living in (or willing to relocate to) either Germany, France, Italy, Serbia, Portugal, or Spain. 
 ➡️ Mission 
 Join us as an  Android Engineer  and help us build the mobile experience that  600,000+ European businesses  rely on every day to manage their finances.   Tackle complex mobile challenges:  You'll contribute to real-time synchronization, resilience patterns, and smooth navigation in a modular codebase with ~1,000 modules.

  Collaborative by nature:  You're fluent in English and contribute through code reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentorship across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  Engineering standards that scale:  Strong code review culture, continuous refactoring, and a focus on correctness in a regulated context. 
  A technically demanding domain:  Fintech constraints — security, compliance, real-time data — push you to solve problems most mobile engineers never encounter. 
 
 ➡️ Our methodology, the  Qonto Way  
 
 We value upfront technical design, team reviews, and smart slicing — quality drives the velocity our customers need. 
 Our org assigns one team lead per project across stacks, giving your team a clear mission and full autonomy on how it operates. 
 Our lean toolbox,  Kaizen  and PDCA, lets you monitor and drive continuous improvement collaboratively with your peers and manager. 
 
 Want to go further? Click  here

 Curious about how we tackle tech debt? Check out our talk from the last Droidcon  here  featuring  Florian .

 As an Android Engineer, you will join one of Qonto's  squad teams , each organised around a  clear project mission , with one team lead and full ownership of a product scope. You'll be part of a  140+ mobile engineering community  within a 500+ Product Engineering department, working in focused  teams of 5 to 10 people  alongside Product, Design, and peers from Frontend and Backend.

9f8c98cd46b1560f.title: Deputy Director of Design Research
9f8c98cd46b1560f.jd:
ABOUT YLABS  
  YLabs is a leading global design and research organization working to improve health and economic opportunity for young people aged 10–24. Founded in 2016 at the Harvard Innovation Lab, YLabs operates across Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Central America in partnership with youth to design products and services addressing key challenges in sexual reproductive health, HIV/AIDS, mental health, financial inclusion, and climate resilience.  
  THE ROLE  
  YLabs is seeking a Deputy Director of Design Research to lead its Deep Listening function and shape the organization- wide vision, methodology, and operational approach to user and ethnographic field research. This role is ideal for a seasoned design researcher who can seamlessly lead projects  from initial research ideation and ground-level field execution to insight synthesis and strategic presentations for C suite executives and senior stakeholders. They will establish institutional systems, develop frameworks across multiple teams, manage Institutional Review Board (IRB) processes, and direct field teams and local Principal Investigators (PIs) across complex regional contexts.  
  JOB TYPE  
  This is a full time position within the Design Department (Job Level: P6 - Deputy Director). The role is scoped for 40 hours per week and is ideally based in East Africa, though candidates within the GMT+0 to GMT+4 time zone on the African continent may also apply. Candidates must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time for field sprints and stakeholder alignment The initial contract term is 12 months, with the possibility of extension.  
  PAY RATE  
  The pay range for this position is   $48,500 - $72,143. This range is regionally benchmarked against the P6 level within YLabs’ Africa salary bands.  YLabs pays all full-time staff salaries in the local currency of the staff member’s permanent work location.   
  KEY RESPONSIBILITIES  
   Research Strategy & Systems Leadership  
 
  Inform and implement the strategic direction for research planning and execution ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and impact goals.  
  Build, scale, and standardize institutional systems, toolkits, and operational blueprints across multiple teams to support effective research ownership and execution.  
  Drive the synthesis of qualitative and quantitative insights across projects to inform high-level strategic decisions, program designs, and organizational growth.  
  Serve as an internal and external subject matter expert, advocating for the critical value of grounded, evidence-based design research.  
 
  IRB, Ethics & Governance Management  
 
  Provide end-to-end oversight and strategic guidance on all Institutional Review Board (IRB) submissions, protocol adaptations, and ethics compliance in collaboration with YLabs Research team  
  Oversee the development of rigorous, ethically sound research protocols (including literature reviews, sampling strategies, and consent mechanisms) tailored to local review board requirements.  
  Manage recruitment and oversight of local Principal Investigators (PIs) to navigate regional regulatory frameworks, cultural nuances, and site approvals.  
  Support development of and ensure strict adherence to Human Subjects standards, global safeguarding policies, and data protection protocols across all field deployments.  
 
  End-to-End Field Execution & Methodological Direction  
 
  Design and lead rapid-cycle field research sprints utilizing immersive observation, semi-structured 1-on-1 interviews, and participatory focus group discussions.  
  Build and manage pipelines for recruiting and training local community researchers and youth field listeners.  
  Oversee t daily field debriefs, implement reflexivity and positionality checks, and mitigate researcher bias during in-person engagements.  
  Adapt research plans dynamically when facing unexpected field obstacles, security considerations, or shifting group dynamics.  
 
  Synthesis, Packaging & Senior Stakeholder Engagement  
 
  Translate raw, complex qualitative field data into structured analytical frameworks, including root-cause analyses, ecosystem maps, personas, and user journey maps.  
  Co-create and iterate insight narratives through participatory sense-making sessions with field teams and local community partners.  
  Synthesise and package research findings into high-impact executive summaries, deep-dive strategic reports, and compelling presentations for donors, C-suite executives, and senior leaders.  
  Translate youth-driven insights into actionable opportunity areas and strategic recommendations for innovation.  
 
  REQUIRED COMPETENCIES  
 
  Design Research & Mixed-Method Research Mastery:   Demonstrates mastery of design research, qualitative and quantitative synthesis, and ethnographic field methods, with proven success in managing multiple complex research projects simultaneously.  
  Autonomy & Strategic Leadership:   Requires no instruction on routine work and operates with complete autonomy on complex organizational initiatives. Makes high-impact strategic decisions independently.  
  IRB & Compliance Expertise:   Deep understanding of ethical research protocols, IRB application processes, informed consent procedures, and human subjects protection.  
  System Building & Prioritization:   Inherently displays best practices in delegation and team management, establishing systems and structures across teams to enable seamless research operations.  
  Adaptability & Complex Problem Solving:   Creatively shifts approaches when facing unexpected field obstacles; demonstrates best practices in navigating barriers and anticipating future challenges.  
  High Emotional Intelligence & Mentorship:   Models best practices in professional relationship building, mentoring team members, managing performance improvements, and navigating sensitive interpersonal dynamics with ease.  
  Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (JEDI):   Models culturally competent ways of working; recognizes and addresses personal and structural biases, creates safe spaces for dialogue, and elevates marginalized voices safely and ethically.  
 
  QUALIFICATIONS  
  Required:  
 
  Minimum of 7 years   of professional experience in design research, user research, qualitative field research, or ethnographic research.Experience conducting such  in the economic empowerment sector is considered an advantage.  
  Demonstrated track record of leading end-to-end design research initiatives—from field immersion and protocol design to executive-level presentation.  
  Proven experience preparing and managing IRB applications and working directly with local PIs, ethics committees, or research approval boards.  
  Demonstrated experience building research systems, toolkits, or operational frameworks used across multiple teams or departments.  
  Substantial experience supervising, training, and mentoring researchers and cross-functional project staff.  
  Exceptional verbal, written, and visual communication skills, with a portfolio showcasing complex research synthesis translated into clear, actionable frameworks  
  Willingness and ability to travel up to 50% of the time to field sites across Sub-Saharan Africa  
  Proficiency with collaborative research synthesis tools (e.g., Miro, Mural, Figma, Dedoose, NVivo).  
 
  Nice to have:  
 
  Master’s or PhD in Anthropology, Design Research, Human-Centered Design, Sociology, UX Research, or a related field.  
  Experience living and working in Sub-Saharan Africa (particularly East Africa).  
  Experience working with vulnerable or marginalized youth populations.  
 
  ADDITIONAL INFORMATION  
  This posting will be open until filled. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis with an expected start date as soon as possible; all applications submitted within the posting period will be reviewed by our Hiring Committee. YLabs recognizes the effort that goes into submitting an application; only successfull candidates will be notified of their application status once the hiring process begins.  
  All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. All YLabs offers of employment are conditional on satisfactory background check and criminal record clearances.

c9b244a83410dee1.title: Full-Stack Product Engineer, AI Tools
c9b244a83410dee1.jd: Meet Aperture    Aperture is a growth consultancy and advertising partner for some of the world's most ambitious ecommerce brands. We plan, build, and manage performance marketing programmes across Meta, TikTok, Google, and beyond — with a strong focus on creative strategy and paid social.   We work across performance marketing, creative strategy, and now, increasingly, proprietary tooling that gives us and our clients an edge.   Founded in 2022 and based across London, we work with clients across the US and Europe. We're a small, senior team that moves fast, thinks carefully, and holds ourselves to a high standard.    Our job is to make growth happen.     Our culture      Client success is our success. Period.   We're direct. We say what we mean and we mean what we say.   We do the work. No one here is above anything.   We hire people we trust and we trust the people we hire.   We move fast, but we don't cut corners where it matters.   We operate with high standards and low ego.   We're here to build something good, not just something big.   We back our people when it counts.      The role    Aperture OS is an internal tool we've built to give us an operational edge. It helps us track performance, manage creative workflows, and surface insights across our client portfolio in ways that off-the-shelf tools don't.   Now we want to scale it.   We're looking for someone to own it. Not manage it. Own it.   You will be the primary engineer and technical decision-maker for Aperture OS. You'll define what it becomes, how it's built, and how it serves the team. You'll work directly with the founder and client teams to understand what's needed and build it — properly.   This is a serious ownership opportunity at a fast-moving company that knows what it wants and gives its people room to deliver it.    What you'll own      The full Aperture OS codebase — architecture, quality, and evolution.   Feature development end-to-end: scoping, building, shipping, iterating.   API integrations — pulling data from ad platforms, creative tools, and internal systems.   AI and LLM integrations — we use AI heavily in our creative and analysis workflows.   Database design and data modelling as the product grows.   Infrastructure, hosting, and deployment — keeping things running reliably.   Security, access control, and compliance for a multi-client environment.      Who this is for    This is for a serious engineer who also builds. You don't wait to be told what to do — you figure it out, propose it, and do it.   You're comfortable with ambiguity and you thrive in environments where the spec isn't always written in advance. You can move quickly when speed is needed and slow down when precision matters.   You care about the product you're building, not just the code. You think about the person using it, the problem it solves, and whether it's actually good.   You've probably worked in a startup or early-stage environment before. You know how to operate without a lot of support infrastructure.   You use AI tools in your daily workflow — not as a crutch, but as a force multiplier. You know when to trust them and when to check the output.   You might have a background in performance marketing, growth, or adtech — or you might not, but you're genuinely curious about it.   If something breaks at 2am and it's your product, you feel it. That's the kind of ownership we're looking for.    How we work    Aperture is remote-first and impact-first.   You can work from wherever you are most productive. We care about the output, not the hours. We do occasional team meetups and we'll bring you in when it makes sense.   You'll have direct access to the founder and the team. No layers, no slow approvals, no bureaucracy.   Requirements     Proven track record shipping with AI-first development tools: Lovable, Cursor, or similar.   Experience owning a full codebase, not just contributing to one.   Strong command of TypeScript and React on the frontend; and serverless/edge functions for backend logic.   Good working knowledge of Supabase for authentication and database (Postgres).   Experience integrating third-party APIs, especially AI and LLM APIs.   Solid working knowledge of DNS, domain management, SSL/TLS, and hosting configuration.   Experience scaling systems in a multi-tenant SaaS environment, with asynchronous processing such as worker fleets, pub/sub, queues and streams.   A sensible approach to testing: you know what needs a test and what doesn't.   You think about security and data compliance as you build, not as an afterthought.   Strong product instincts: you know the difference between something that works and something that is right.   Ability to set priorities and make tradeoffs without constant direction.   Familiarity with performance marketing, ad creative testing, or growth tooling.     Benefits     Work from anywhere, with flexibility around how you structure your day.   Regular team meetups and events.   Travel to team meetups covered.   Direct exposure to a fast-growing business and its founder.   Real ownership of a product people use every day.   A high-trust role with responsibility from day one.

3053a81706fafe8c.title: Product Growth (apps)
3053a81706fafe8c.jd: Role Overview - Product Growth (Apps)  Aperture is a growth consultancy and advertising partner for some of the world's most ambitious ecommerce and consumer brands. We plan, build, and manage performance marketing programmes across Meta, TikTok, Google, and beyond - with a strong focus on paid social and creative strategy.  We work at the intersection of creative, media, and product. Our clients trust us to drive real business outcomes — not just ad performance - which means we care deeply about what happens after the click.  Founded in 2022 and based across London, we're a small, senior team that moves fast, thinks carefully, and holds ourselves to a high standard.   Our culture    Client success is our success. Period.  We're direct. We say what we mean and we mean what we say.  We do the work. No one here is above anything.  We hire people we trust and we trust the people we hire.  We move fast, but we don't cut corners where it matters.  We operate with high standards and low ego.  We're here to build something good, not just something big.  We back our people when it counts.    The role   Growth at Aperture means owning the full post-acquisition funnel itself. You'll be the person who asks: now that we've got them, what do we do with them?  This is a senior, high-ownership role. You'll be responsible for the thinking and execution behind onboarding, activation, conversion, and retention. You understand the difference between a user who "completed signup" and a user who was actually activated. You know that the commitment screen is not a paywall - it's a product moment. And you know that ARPU is a vanity metric if you haven't thought about ARPPU.  You'll work directly with our founder and our client teams, shaping the growth strategies we bring to clients and building the frameworks that make Aperture's approach to growth distinctive and defensible.   What you'll own    Onboarding flow strategy - designing and optimising the first-use experience to drive activation, not just registration  Activation frameworks - defining what "activated" means for each product or client, and building the system to get users there  Commitment screen and paywall strategy - copy, structure, timing, and A/B testing to maximise conversion without eroding trust  Monetisation strategy - pricing presentation, upsell sequencing, trial-to-paid mechanics, and expansion revenue thinking  Retention and lifecycle - cohort analysis, churn identification, win-back programmes, and engagement loops that sustain ARPU over time  A/B testing culture - building a rigorous, fast-moving experimentation practice with proper statistical thinking  Client-facing growth audits - reviewing client funnels end-to-end and delivering actionable recommendations      Who this is for   You've worked in apps and subscriptions, and you've had direct ownership of funnel metrics. You're not a generalist who's dabbled in product - you're someone who has spent serious time thinking about activation and why some users stick while others don't.  You think in systems. You can break down a funnel, identify the highest-leverage intervention point, and build a test to validate your hypothesis - all before lunchtime. You're as comfortable in a spreadsheet as you are in a strategy deck.  You understand that the best growth work is invisible to users: it's not tricks or dark patterns, it's removing friction, reinforcing value, and making the right next step obvious at every moment.   Requirements   Experience & Qualifications   Proven experience owning onboarding and activation for a consumer app, SaaS product, or subscription business  Track record of materially improving activation rates or reducing time-to-value through structured experimentation  Deep understanding of paywall and commitment screen mechanics - you can articulate why the same offer converts differently depending on framing, timing, and context  Fluent in ARPU, ARPPU, LTV, payback period, and the relationships between them; you know when each metric matters and when it misleads  Experience running a rigorous A/B testing programme - you understand statistical significance, novelty effects, and when to stop a test  Strong cohort analysis skills - you can identify churn inflection points, segment by activation status, and model the impact of funnel changes  Familiarity with behavioural psychology principles that underpin good onboarding (progress mechanics, social proof, loss aversion, commitment and consistency)  Client-facing communication skills - you can translate funnel analysis into clear strategic recommendations for a non-technical audience  Comfortable working across product, data, and marketing - this role spans all three   Nice to have   Experience with ecommerce conversion and post-purchase monetisation (upsell, subscriptions, loyalty)  Familiarity with analytics tools: Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog, Braze, or similar  Understanding of paid acquisition mechanics — you know how upstream CAC decisions affect downstream LTV  Experience building growth frameworks that others can use, not just doing the work yourself   How we work  Work from anywhere, with flexibility around how you structure your day.  Direct exposure to high-growth clients and meaningful work.  Regular team meetups and retreats, with travel covered.  Access to conferences, events and industry sessions.  Small team, high ownership, fast progression.    Before you apply  We read every single application.  We ask a few questions as part of the process. This is where we understand how you think.  We’re not looking for perfect answers. We’re looking for real ones.  Specific examples matter more than polished language.  We can tell when something is generic.  Take your time. Write from your own experience.

25f33aaf0528fc88.title: Product Growth (Monetisation) Manager
25f33aaf0528fc88.jd: Meet Aperture  Aperture is a growth consultancy and advertising partner for ambitious apps, platforms and digital products.  We work across performance marketing, creative strategy, product optimisation, CRM, analytics and experimentation to help companies scale. Our clients rely on us to identify the biggest growth opportunities, turn them into well-designed experiments and deliver measurable commercial impact.  Our job is to make growth happen.  The role  We’re looking for a Monetisation Manager with deep, hands-on experience growing subscription-based mobile apps.  You will lead monetisation strategy and experimentation across a portfolio of clients, working across onboarding, paywalls, pricing, plans, trials, offers, product gating, retention and cancellation.  You must have personally configured and run experiments in both RevenueCat and Adapty, understand how the platforms work in detail and be confident diagnosing problems when the data or implementation does not behave as expected.  You’ll combine commercial thinking, customer understanding, product analytics and rigorous experimentation to help clients increase revenue without sacrificing retention or long-term value.   Requirements   What you’ll own   Audit clients’ monetisation models, subscription infrastructure, funnels, analytics and experiment history, then build prioritised roadmaps.  Personally configure and manage products, entitlements, offerings, paywalls, placements, audiences, targeting and experiments in RevenueCat and Adapty.  Lead experimentation across pricing, plans, trials, offers, onboarding, paywalls, product gating, localisation, cancellation and web-to-app journeys.  Design rigorous tests with clear hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, audiences, traffic allocation and decision criteria.  Analyse the full subscription funnel, from conversion and trial-to-paid through renewal, churn, revenue and LTV, identifying misleading results and meaningful differences between cohorts.  Reconcile data across RevenueCat, Adapty, the app stores, product analytics, attribution platforms and warehouse data, resolving tracking or implementation issues with technical teams.  Turn behavioural data, customer research and commercial insight into stronger propositions and experiments, working with design, product, engineering, analytics and CRM teams to launch and QA them.  Present clear recommendations and results to clients, documenting every experiment and contributing reusable learnings to Aperture OS.   What we’re looking for   Significant experience monetising consumer subscription apps across iOS and Android, with a proven impact on conversion, revenue or retention.  Deep, hands-on expertise in RevenueCat and Adapty, including personally configuring subscription products, paywalls and experiments.  Strong knowledge of App Store and Google Play subscriptions and rigorous A/B testing, from experiment design and sample size through to revenue maturity.  Excellent analytical and commercial judgement, including the ability to interpret funnel data, distinguish short-term conversion gains from genuine LTV growth and diagnose tracking issues.  Clear, confident client communication and a proactive approach to managing multiple workstreams, dependencies and blockers.   Particularly valuable experience   Superwall, Purchasely or similar monetisation platforms.  Product analytics tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, Firebase or PostHog, plus SQL or event-level analysis.  Web-to-app monetisation, localisation, cancellation flows and churn reduction.  Working across multiple clients in a consultancy or agency environment.   What success looks like  Within your first few months, you will have:   Established clear monetisation baselines and prioritised experimentation roadmaps for your clients.  Launched rigorous tests through RevenueCat and Adapty across pricing, paywalls, onboarding and retention.  Improved the reliability of monetisation data and the quality of experiment decisions.  Turned results into actionable recommendations and reusable learnings for clients and Aperture OS.   How we work   Client success is our success.  We take ownership of outcomes and raise blockers early.  We use evidence to make decisions and focus on measurable impact.  We communicate directly, thoughtfully and without ego.  We document what we learn so every experiment makes the next one smarter.

fb20d135f11ab1fb.jd:
BRND WGN  
  —  
  We're a team fuelled by strategic thinking and creativity, dedicated to helping entrepreneurs craft meaningful brands that positively impact our world. We aid these brands in developing robust strategies, impactful designs, successful campaigns, engaging content, web development, and exceptional UX/UI. We also create bold brand experiences that make their names stand out.  
   
  Our approach is defined by curiosity, simplifying complexities, and prioritising clarity. Our thinking leads us to do the unexpected and our approach makes room for powerful ideas. Our disruptive ways challenge the norm to deliver results, each and every time.  
   
  Our Principles:  
  👩🏻‍🎤  Challenge everything     💙  Be brutally honest     💪🏼  Find a way     🏆  We win together  
   
  A New Global Chapter:  
  BRND WGN is building a dedicated team that will work directly with nmbl, a New York–based creative agency delivering world-class work for global brands such as   Nespresso, Canon, and Vital Proteins.  
   
  This collaboration gives our new team the opportunity to operate on fast-paced, high-impact international projects while being fully supported by BRND WGN’s strategic and creative culture.  
   
   
  THE POSITION  
  —  
  We're on the lookout for a   Graphic Designer   to join our expanding creative team.

They will work across multiple projects and clients—creating brand assets, campaign visuals, digital layouts, and content systems that feel intentional, crafted, and aligned with strategic direction.  
   
  With a strong visual eye and adaptable design approach, they can shift easily between concepting, execution, and refinement. Working closely with Creative, Strategy, and Content teams, they ensure that every output feels cohesive and contributes to a brand’s wider visual ecosystem.  
   
  Responsibilities:  
 
  Design brand and campaign assets across digital, social, video, and traditional platforms.  
  Develop and evolve content templates, toolkits, and visual systems for ongoing use.  
  Collaborate with Strategists, Copywriters, Editors, and Creatives to translate ideas into design.

  Ensure visual consistency across brands, workstreams, and deliverables.  
  Embody nmbl’s principles — collaboration, curiosity, honesty, and a solution-driven mindset.  
 
   
  Requirements:  
 
  3–5 years  experience in graphic design, digital design, or brand identity.  
  Advanced proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite and Figma (motion tools a plus).  
  Strong grasp of typography, layout, hierarchy, and systems thinking.  
  Ability to work within evolving brand worlds while contributing fresh ideas.  
  Comfortable juggling multiple brands, timelines, and deliverables.  
  Experience preparing assets for digital and social platforms.  
 
   
  Conditions:  
 
  Working Hours:   This role is aligned with our US-based team and requires availability within an approximate 7:00am–5:00pm ET coverage window.   
  Travel Budget:   €2,000 annual travel budget (work-related travel, team meet-ups, and collaboration with our US partners)  
  Location:   Hybrid (The Brewhouse, Malta / Remote)  
  Salary Range:   €30,000 — €40,000 annually (depending on experience)  
 
   
   
  THE PERKS

dee27d5ed937e5d3.title: Senior Product Designer
dee27d5ed937e5d3.jd: RemoFirst  is transforming the way businesses hire and manage global teams. We partner with some of the world’s most innovative companies, including Fortune 500 businesses and leading startups. What you will be doing    User and Business Research and Analysis:   Conduct research and analyze user and business needs to create effective interfaces with a focus on onboarding journeys.   Gather and interpret user feedback and data to inform design decisions. Wireframing, Layout, and Design:   Create wireframes, layouts, and designs that meet user requirements and business goals, with strong creativity in UI to enhance onboarding flows and AI feature interactions. e53fae0e2d514bcd.title: Director, Product Design
e53fae0e2d514bcd.jd: Director Product Design     Europe / Remote  Reports to the Chief Strategy and Product Officer     About Velsera    Velsera builds software that turns complex biological data into research insight and clinical answers. Our platforms work across multi-omic and multi-modal data: genomics alongside proteomics, transcriptomics and other omics, together with imaging, clinical and real-world data, at the scale of some of the world's largest biomedical programs. Pharmaceutical companies, biotechs, public research initiatives and diagnostic laboratories use our products to advance precision medicine.   We run like a scale-up: small teams with real authority, fast decisions, and AI woven into how we work day to day. We measure ourselves on impact for our customers and, ultimately, for patients.    The opportunity    You'd be joining as the design authority for our Seven Bridges Platform and the leader of design at Velsera, just as we rebuild how we design, validate and ship. You report directly to the Chief Strategy and Product Officer, and decisions that take quarters elsewhere happen here in days. Our product managers have already started turning ideas into working, on-brand prototypes with AI and put them in front of customers within weeks. The design foundations that make that speed safe are yours to build and own: design tokens, a component library, and the patterns everyone works with.   That's the shape of your influence here. Product managers prototype with the system you build, you review what customers will see, and once a concept is validated, production design belongs to you: journeys that hold up across every state, edge case and installation. This is a product bioinformaticians, scientists and clinicians rely on every day, and you set its bar.   This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll manage our product designer working on the clinical side of our portfolio, you'll build the design function as it grows, and you'll keep doing the craft yourself. There's no large design team to inherit; there's one to create.   The product is changing as fast as the craft is. Our users increasingly work alongside AI in research and diagnostic workflows, with dense, high-stakes data from many sources. Someone needs to rethink the journeys, trust models and information design of software like ours for that reality. That is a key remit of this job.   This role won't suit everyone. If you're looking for a mature design organization with settled processes, you won't find that here yet. If you want to build the system a whole company designs with, lead design for products with real clinical stakes, and do it at scale-up speed, we should talk.      What will you do?    Own the user journeys, flows and interaction design of the Seven Bridges Platform: partner with product managers on problems, outcomes and scope, then own how the experience actually works, from structure and states down to the number of clicks.     Build our design system from the ground up: design tokens, a component library aligned with our front-end code, and the standards that bring our product surfaces together under one visual language. The whole organization will prototype with what you build.     Keep rapid prototyping fast and safe: maintain the foundations PMs build with, review prototype quality before customers see it, and take validated prototypes through to production-ready design.     Manage our product designer on the clinical side: set goals, develop their craft, give honest feedback, and answer for the quality of design across both businesses. As the team grows, you'll hire and shape it.     Design for AI in the product itself: assistant and copilot experiences, AI-generated results that scientists and clinicians can trust and verify, and workflows where automation and human judgment work together.     Work closely with front-end engineers so the design system lives in code, not only in Figma.     Use product analytics to see where users struggle, make experience debt visible, and give product leadership a clear case for what to fix first.     Bring design judgment into strategy conversations at the leadership level.       Your first few months    The first version of the design system is live, with tokens and core components in Figma and in code, and product managers are actually prototyping on top of it. You've reviewed working prototypes before they went in front of real customers, and what we shipped is better for it. You and the designer you manage have a real working rhythm, with clear goals and honest feedback, and it shows in the work. And your map of our experience debt is on the leadership table with a clear case for what to fix first.    Requirements    What do you bring to the table?   You've spent seven or more years in product design, with senior ownership of user journeys on complex, data-heavy or scientific software.    You've built or led at least one design system that engineering genuinely adopted, and you know what it takes to keep one alive.     You've managed designers formally, not just mentored them, and the people you've managed got better and would work for you again.     You're comfortable having your biggest impact through a system other people build with, not only through screens you designed yourself.     You've chosen fast, ambiguous environments before, and you're looking for another one.     You already use AI tools to design, prototype and produce working software (we work with Claude, from design exploration through design-to-code), and you have well-formed opinions about where these tools help and where they mislead.     You've designed AI-powered product experiences, or you have a clear point of view on trust, transparency and human oversight in AI interfaces.     You're an expert in Figma, including variables and design-to-code workflows such as Code Connect.     You know enough front-end to collaborate credibly with engineers on components and constraints. You don't need to write production code, but you do need to understand how your designs become it.     You can operate as the most senior design voice in the company: comfortable with ambiguity, generous as a coach, and clear whether you're talking to executives, engineers or scientists.    Nice to have: experience with genomics, multi-omics, imaging, clinical or other life sciences data products, or another regulated domain; products delivered across multiple environments or installations; familiarity with component documentation tools like Storybook; experience establishing design practice in an engineering-led organization.       Why this position?   You get real authority over a core product and the design function itself, from day one, with a direct line to the Chief Strategy and Product Officer. You join a company that works the way it's asking you to work: AI-assisted, fast and hands-on. The work ends in research results and patient outcomes, which makes the pace worth it. And you won't inherit a design practice here; you'll build the one everyone after you inherits.    Benefits    Flexible Work & Time Off - Embrace hybrid work models and enjoy the freedom of unlimited paid time off to support work-life balance.  Health & Well-being - Access comprehensive group medical and life insurance coverage, along with a 24/7 Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental health and wellness support.  Growth & Learning - Fuel your professional journey with continuous learning and development programs designed to help you upskill and grow.  Engaging & Fun Work Culture - Experience a vibrant workplace with team events, celebrations, and engaging activities that make every workday enjoyable.  & Many More...

df23e418ad147021.title: Product Designer (Trading)
df23e418ad147021.jd: We’re building the next generation of TN Trader — a proprietary, React-based trading platform designed for the needs of global CFD and spread betting traders. Our commitments to each other    We have each other’s backs   There when we need each other most   We challenge each other   Be more creative, more curious, more bold   We thrive together   Taking our work to the next level   We form strong bonds   Through team building and social events   We don’t judge   Instead, we teach and are open to learning   We step up   Taking ownership and supporting each other to do the same    Responsibilities   Own the brief-to-delivery pipeline: receive briefs from business stakeholders, resolve ambiguity proactively, and confirm deliverables, format and success criteria before a single pixel is placed. f722d4e31136103b.title: Product Designer (B2B)
f722d4e31136103b.jd: TryHackMe is the fastest-growing online cyber security training platform. Our mission is to make learning and teaching cyber security easier by providing gamified security exercises and challenges. Having only been around for handful of years, we've grown to more than 8 million community members and our growth isn't slowing down! 🥷  About the role   Own the design of the product thousands of organisations use to develop their cybersecurity teams.   TryHackMe takes people from cybersecurity beginner to job-ready through hands-on, gamified learning. More than 8 million people have learned with us - and thousands of companies now use TryHackMe to train their security teams.  That B2B product is where you come in. We're hiring a Product Designer to own the core B2B experience end to end: how organisations get started, how admins run their training programmes, and how it all hangs together. You'll design new features and improve what's already there, with a clear goal - deeper engagement and stronger adoption.  The role  You'll partner closely with Product Managers and Engineers across the teams building the core B2B experience: onboarding flows, the admin dashboard, and the business-specific features our growing customer base depends on. You'll also work with the B2C teams so the learning experience stays consistent, whether someone's on TryHackMe individually or as part of their company's team. 7e733c1886377326.title: Product Engineer
7e733c1886377326.jd: 🤝 About us  FounderNest is an AI-native company helping corporations understand markets and generate strategic insights from complex data.  We work with a dataset of 50M+ companies and 1.2B+ data points, combining real-time analytics, search, and Generative AI to deliver high-quality, explainable insights.  We build production-grade LLM systems, retrieval pipelines, internal agents, and evaluation frameworks designed to operate reliably at scale for the core infrastructure of our product.  Our product is used by hundreds of customers daily, including large enterprises like Bloomberg and Shiseido.  📍  Location   Fully remote within Spain only. Candidates must currently reside in Spain and have legal authorization to work in Spain.  🎯 The role  You would join our  GTM Engineering  team, where your closest teammates would be engineers and people from product, marketing and sales.  Our job is to automate the repetitive, mechanical work in sales, marketing and customer success, so those teams spend their time on the things only a human can do: closing deals, nurturing prospects, and building the relationships that turn into upsells. We do that through experimentation, scrappy by design: find the shortest path to something that works, put it in front of people who will use it, learn and keep going.  In practice:     Find where the most expensive friction is and build the thing that removes it , usually before the person drowning in it has to ask for help.     Build it end-to-end, mostly on the backend:  integrations with the tools our teams already use, data pipelines, LLM-powered workflows, and whatever interface makes it usable.     Be measured on the outcome : leads, meetings booked, revenue generated.    A few things stand out about this role. Very few engineers get to draw a straight line from something they built to money the company made. The feedback loop is short: you ship on Tuesday, someone is using it on Wednesday, by Friday you know whether it worked. And you’ll work on AI systems in production from day one.  🧩 What we are looking for  We are not hiring for a specific seniority, but you’ll need around 2 years of professional experience shipping software. Beyond that, how you think matters more than your title.     You are either full-stack or strong on the backend.  Most of this work (integrations with APIs and SDKs, data pipelines, LLMs) lives on the backend, so that is where we need you to be solid. Knowing your way around the frontend, or being up for learning it, is a plus.     You take ownership of problems, not tickets.  You want to know who the user is and what actually helps them before you start building, and here you can just ask, because they’re one Slack message away.     You are lean and pragmatic . You would rather ship something small and useful this week than something perfect next quarter. You choose solutions proportional to the problem, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made.     You can work with people who are not engineers , explaining your reasoning without jargon, and taking a half-formed request from someone in sales and turning it into a real problem statement.     You pick things up fast and you like doing it . Most of what this role needs you can learn here.    👉  Nice to have.  Two things would make you stand out:     AI engineering . You have taken an AI-powered feature to production and know what breaks once real users touch it.     AI-assisted coding . You get real leverage out of coding agents, to the point where you are directing and reviewing the work rather than typing it.    🛠️ Our stack  TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, BigQuery, AWS, LangChain, LangSmith, New Relic  💰 Compensation & Perks     Permanent full-time contract .     Competitive salary , reviewed as you grow with us.     Stock options , so you share in the upside as the company grows.     Latest equipment  you need to work comfortably from home.     Flexible schedule , have the freedom to organize your day.     Unlimited vacation policy , take the time you need to recharge.     90/10 policy : Devote 10% of you time (usually a Friday every other week) to innovate and learn.     Birthday policy : we celebrate your day with a special gift.

Contribute to Practice Development:  Support the evolution of the UX practice,  including how it interfaces with the emerging AX (Agentic Experience) discipline,  and provide training to empower other teams in adopting design best practices. Either a degree in a UX related field and professional experience with complex products (B2B SaaS preferred).      Experience working in the technology industry.      Working knowledge of how AI copilots, assistants, or agents are changing product experiences,  enough fluency to spot when a feature you're designing has an agent in the loop, and to have an informed conversation with AX and AI teams about it.      Familiarity with the UX - UAX - AX spectrum (human-navigated, human-and-agent co-navigated, and agent-autonomous experiences) as a way of framing where a given design problem sits.      Great communication skills, including the ability to explain human-centered design needs to technical and AI-focused stakeholders. d6d6cd92049399ab.title: UX & Product Design Lead
d6d6cd92049399ab.jd: About bunny.net   Some people accept the internet as it is. We see what it could be.  At bunny.net, we don’t wait for change. We make it happen. You won’t find layers of red tape or play-it-safe thinking here. You’ll find people who move quickly, take ownership, and push ideas all the way to the edge. Literally.  You’ll build things that solve actual problems, not add to them.  We’re not perfect, and we don’t pretend to be. But we’re always improving. We’re looking for people who want to do the same, who take pride in their work, and aren’t afraid to challenge what’s possible.  Because everyone deserves a better internet. And we’re here to help it hop faster.    UX & Product Design Lead   The internet runs on infrastructure. But using that infrastructure shouldn't feel... well, like infrastructure.  That's where you come in.  As our UX & Product Design Lead, you'll help shape how developers experience bunny.net.  Working closely with product managers and engineers, you'll own the UX journey from early product ideas through to polished experiences developers love using.  This isn't a role where you'll approve every mockup. You'll be hands-on where it matters most, solving meaningful product challenges while building the systems, patterns, and culture that help great UX scale across bunny.net.  You'll spend your time experimenting with new ideas, using AI to move faster, and continuously refining the experiences we build.  The best UX often goes unnoticed, because everything just works.  If that excites you, you'll feel right at home.   What will you do?     Make powerful technology feel beautifully simple    Shape the experience of products used by developers around the world    Work side by side with product managers and engineers to solve tough problems    Build the systems and design patterns that help great UX scale    Prototype, experiment, and explore with AI and modern design tools    Lead and set standards for user research and define the personas that guide every design decision    Talk to customers often, and let their feedback shape what we build    Bring clarity to complex product decisions through design workshops and reviews    Raise the bar for usability, accessibility, and thoughtful product design    Help others become better designers by sharing knowledge, giving feedback, and leading by example     What will you bring?     7+ years of experience in UX, product design, or a similar role    Experience designing cloud infrastructure, and/or products for developers    Confidence designing for technical users, especially developers    Ability to conduct qualitative and quantitative user research    A talent for turning technical complexity into intuitive experiences    Systems thinking: you know when to solve a problem once, and when to create a pattern that solves it for everyone    The ability to zoom out to strategy and dive into the details when it matters    A collaborative mindset and the ability to work closely with engineers to balance user needs with technical realities    Clear communication and the confidence to explain your thinking to anyone, from engineers to leadership    Curiosity about AI and modern tools, and a desire to keep improving how products are designed and built    An obsession with the little details that make powerful products feel fast, simple, and effortless     What will make us extra happy?     Experience building design systems, component libraries, or design tokens    Familiarity with frontend technologies like HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or Angular    Experience designing for APIs, cloud platforms, infrastructure, security, or other developer tools    Experience using AI to accelerate research, prototyping, or product design    Experience mentoring designers or helping scale design practices in a product organization      Where should you be located?    Europe, ideally within CET ±3 hours so collaboration with the team feels natural rather than scheduled.    What's in it for you?   Life at bunny.net comes with benefits that make work (and life) better.     100% flexible hours -  Your work, your rhythm. Whether you thrive at 3 am or on a beach at noon, we've got you.     Remote-first by design  - No offices, no commute, just the freedom to work anywhere. Miss the office? We’ll give you a 3-night voucher for visiting our  headquarters .     Medical, dental, and vision insurance -  Coverage worldwide.     Paid time off -  Love the slopes or the sea? Enjoy them with 25 vacation days, plus an extra loyalty day each year, capped at 5 years (30 days total), on top of your local public holidays.     Meeting-free Thursdays  - We keep Thursdays meeting free internally so you can focus on deep work without interruptions.     Home office budget -  We believe everyone is more efficient working in a comfortable office, and we're happy to help you set it up with an annual budget of €500.     Paid sick leave -  Feeling ill? Take time off to fully recover without having to worry about your finances.     Parental leave -  Paid 16 weeks for birthing parents, 8 weeks for non-birthing parents. If your country gives more, that’s your baseline. If it gives less, we top it up. Take your leave all at once or split it across the first year for maximum flexibility. After paid leave, your local statutory rules apply.     Annual fluffle building  - We're remote, but not distant! Once a year, we meet in a sunny location where virtual high-fives turn into real ones.     Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP)  - Everyone at bunny.net gets a piece of the pie, starting with 0.01% equity.     Mental health support -  Feeling down? We've got your back. bunny.net provides mental health resources and help via   BetterHelp.com  .     Wellness budget -  An annual well-being budget of €480 is here to help you stay fresh and focused.     Educational budget -  €500 yearly for books, seminars, or online courses to keep your learning on track, work-related or not.     Music on us:  Work is better with music. Enjoy a yearly Apple, Spotify, or YouTube Premium subscription on us.
